title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Kiribati: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Kiribati: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Kiribati: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in Kiribati. Below, we set out the five official administrative and legal steps in chronological order - covering medical certification, civil registration, burial or international repatriation, social security and financial notifications, and succession before the courts in Kiribati.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Cause of Death
steps.html:
• Hospital or clinic deaths: When a death occurs at Tungaru Central Hospital in Nawerewere (South Tarawa), Southern Kiribati Hospital, Betio Hospital, London Hospital on Kiritimati, or an outer-island health centre operated by the Ministry of Health and Medical Services, the attending medical officer or qualified medical assistant examines the deceased and issues the official Medical Certificate of Cause of Death [1][2].
  • Deaths at home or on outer islands: If your family member died at home in a village (maneaba community) without a doctor present, notify the nearest Island Health Centre or medical assistant under the Ministry of Health and Medical Services so the death can be medically verified and recorded [2]. Where no medical practitioner attended the deceased during their final illness, the local island registrar and village headman or island council officer record the circumstances of death under the Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Ordinance (Cap. 5) [1].
  • Sudden, accidental, or unexplained deaths: If the death was unexpected, violent, unnatural, or occurred under unknown circumstances, report it immediately to the Kiribati Police Service. A magistrate exercises statutory inquiry powers under the Magistrates' Courts Ordinance (Cap. 52) and orders a post-mortem examination before a burial or cremation clearance is granted [2][5].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Civil Registry
steps.html:
• Statutory authority and where to file: Civil registration of deaths is governed by the Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Ordinance (Cap. 5) and administered nationally by the Civil Registration Office within the Ministry of Justice in Ambo, South Tarawa, or through the designated District Registrar at each Island Council on the outer islands and in the Line and Phoenix Islands [1][3].
  • Statutory deadline and required informants: Under the Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Ordinance (Cap. 5), the nearest relative present at the death or in attendance during the last illness - or, if none is available, any occupier of the house or person arranging the burial - must register the death with the Registrar within 10 days of the event [1][3].
  • Documents required and certified extracts: Bring the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death, the deceased's birth certificate, national identity card or passport, and marriage certificate (if applicable) to the Ministry of Justice or Island Council Registrar [1][3]. Once the entry is recorded in the Register of Deaths, request multiple certified copies of the official Death Certificate for pension, banking, and court probate filings [3].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Local burial and public health rules: Burials in Kiribati are regulated under the Public Health Ordinance (Cap. 80) and local Urban Council (Betio Town Council or Teinainano Urban Council on South Tarawa) or Island Council bylaws [2][6]. A burial permit or medical clearance certificate must be obtained before interment in a designated cemetery or approved family plot [1][6].
  • Mortuary services and local coordination: Tungaru Central Hospital under the Ministry of Health and Medical Services maintains mortuary storage facilities on South Tarawa and coordinates cold storage, preparation of remains, and sanitary clearance [2][6].
  • International repatriation and document legalisation: If the deceased was a foreign citizen or if remains must be repatriated abroad, the Ministry of Health and Medical Services issues a non-infectious disease certificate and embalming/sealing clearance in accordance with international aviation and public health rules [2][6]. Because Kiribati is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, Kiribati death certificates used abroad must undergo diplomatic or consular authentication through the Ministry of Justice and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Immigration, followed by legalisation at the relevant foreign high commission or embassy [3].

steps.title: Notify Provident Fund, Pension, Tax, and Banking Authorities
steps.html:
• Kiribati Provident Fund death benefit and account settlement: If your family member was an active or former contributor to the Kiribati Provident Fund, surviving nominated beneficiaries or legal representatives should file a Death Claim with the Kiribati Provident Fund head office in Bairiki, South Tarawa (or its Kiritimati branch) [4]. Submit the official Death Certificate, proof of identity for each nominated beneficiary, and the deceased's member details to claim the accumulated member balance and any applicable statutory funeral or death grant [4].
  • Senior citizens allowance and public benefits: If the deceased received the national Elderly Fund (Kara) monthly allowance or disability support through the Ministry of Women, Youth, Sport and Social Affairs, notify the ministry or the local Island Council welfare officer to close the benefit file and avoid overpayment recovery [3].
  • Banks, tax, and identity cancellations: Present the certified Death Certificate from the Ministry of Justice to ANZ Kiribati or the Development Bank of Kiribati to freeze sole accounts and verify balance statements, and notify the Kiribati Internal Revenue Board if the deceased held a registered business or salaried tax account [3].

steps.title: Administer the Estate, Succession, and Land Probate
steps.html:
• Succession to native land vs. personal estate: Under Kiribati law and the Magistrates' Courts Ordinance (Cap. 52), succession to customary native land and real property rights is adjudicated by the Magistrates' Court (sitting in its Lands Division) in accordance with the Gilbert and Phoenix Islands Lands Code, which sets out customary inheritance rules for children, spouses, and extended kin [5].
  • High Court probate and letters of administration: For larger non-customary estates, commercial assets, or contested wills, applications for a Grant of Probate (when the deceased left a valid will) or Letters of Administration (when the deceased died intestate) are filed with the High Court of Kiribati in Betio or through the judicial registry overseen by the Ministry of Justice [3][5].
  • Taxation and cross-border coordination: Kiribati does not levy a separate statutory inheritance or estate tax on personal property passing to heirs. If heirs live outside Kiribati or if the estate includes overseas bank accounts, foreign powers of attorney and court grants must be authenticated via consular legalisation before presentation to the High Court or local financial institutions [3][5].

closingQuestion: To help us tailor this checklist to your exact situation, did the death occur on South Tarawa or an outer island, and did your family member hold an active account with the Kiribati Provident Fund or own customary land in Kiribati?
